# Sales / Challans

This document describes the Sales Challan module: fields, workflow, status transitions,
permissions, stock behavior, cancellation/reversal, APIs, and the assumptions made where the
case study and this project's own planning docs left details unspecified.

No schema changes were made for this feature — the existing `Challan` and `ChallanItem`
Prisma models (from the original database foundation) already covered every CHL-001–009
requirement.

## Fields

**Challan**: `id, challanNumber (auto-generated, unique, format CH-000001), customerId, status
(DRAFT | CONFIRMED | CANCELLED), totalQuantity, createdById, createdAt, confirmedAt, updatedAt`.
`totalAmount` is **not** persisted — it's calculated on every read as
`SUM(ChallanItem.lineTotal)` and attached to API responses as a derived `totalAmount` field.

**ChallanItem** (one challan → many items, one per product): `id, challanId, productId,
productNameSnapshot, productSkuSnapshot, unitPriceSnapshot, quantity, lineTotal`. The
`*Snapshot` fields are frozen at the moment the item is created/edited — a challan's item list
never changes retroactively if the underlying `Product`'s name, SKU, or price changes later.

## Workflow

```
Sales/Admin picks a Customer
        ↓
Adds one or more Product + Quantity lines (no duplicate products per challan)
        ↓
Saves as DRAFT, or Confirms immediately (POST /api/challans with status=CONFIRMED)
        ↓
DRAFT can be: edited (customer/items), confirmed, or cancelled (no stock effect)
        ↓
Confirming: re-validates every line (product exists, is active, has enough stock),
deducts stock atomically for ALL lines in one transaction, records one StockMovement (OUT)
per line linked to the challan, sets status=CONFIRMED and confirmedAt
        ↓
CONFIRMED can be cancelled: stock is restored for every line via StockMovement (IN)
records linked to the same challan, status becomes CANCELLED
        ↓
CANCELLED is terminal: read-only, no further edits, confirms, or cancels
```

## Status transitions

| From | To | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| DRAFT | CONFIRMED | Stock deducted (all lines, atomically); `confirmedAt` set |
| DRAFT | CANCELLED | No stock change |
| CONFIRMED | CANCELLED | Stock **restored** for every line (reversal `StockMovement` IN records) |
| CANCELLED | *(any)* | Rejected — cancelled challans are terminal |
| CONFIRMED | *(edit)* | Rejected — only DRAFT challans can be edited |

## Stock behavior

Confirming a challan re-validates, in order, for every line: the product still exists, is
still `isActive`, and has `currentStock >= quantity` — using the same atomic
conditional-update pattern (`updateMany` with a `WHERE currentStock >= quantity` guard) proven
under concurrency in the Inventory module. If **any** line fails any check, the entire
transaction throws and Postgres rolls back everything — no line item's stock is touched, the
challan's status is unaffected, and the client gets a `409` naming the failing product.

The same atomic guard protects the status transition itself: confirming does
`UPDATE challans SET status='CONFIRMED' WHERE id=? AND status='DRAFT'` before touching any
stock, so two concurrent confirm requests on the same challan can't both succeed — only one
wins, the other gets `409`.

## Cancellation / stock reversal

- **DRAFT → CANCELLED**: trivial, no stock was ever deducted.
- **CONFIRMED → CANCELLED**: every `ChallanItem`'s quantity is added back to its product's
  `currentStock`, and a reversal `StockMovement` (`movementType: IN`, `challanId` set, reason
  `"Challan <number> cancelled — stock reversal"`) is created per line — so the audit trail
  shows both the original OUT deduction and the reversal IN, both linked to the challan.
  Guarded the same way as confirm (atomic conditional status transition), so a cancel racing a
  confirm, or two concurrent cancels, can't both apply.

## Challan numbering

Format `CH-000001`, `CH-000002`, ... — generated by reading the highest existing
`challanNumber` and incrementing. Since adding a database sequence would require a migration
(explicitly out of scope), correctness under concurrent creates comes from a retry loop: if two
requests compute the same "next" number, the database's unique constraint on `challanNumber`
rejects the second `INSERT`, and that whole creation attempt is retried (up to 5 times) with a
freshly-computed number. Verified under a 4-way concurrent-create test — all 4 succeed with
distinct sequential numbers.

## Permissions

Approved role matrix:

| Action | ADMIN | SALES | WAREHOUSE | ACCOUNTS |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| View challans | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Create challans | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ |
| Edit DRAFT challans | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ |
| Confirm challans | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ |
| Cancel challans | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ |

Enforced server-side via `authenticate` + `requireRole` on every route (unchanged middleware,
reused as-is). The frontend also hides write actions (New/Edit/Confirm/Cancel buttons) from
WAREHOUSE/ACCOUNTS users for UX — but this is presentation only; every write endpoint
independently re-checks the role server-side regardless of what the UI shows.

## APIs

All endpoints are under `/api/challans` and require `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/challans` | List, paginated, with `status`/`customerId`/`search`/`dateFrom`/`dateTo` filters |
| POST | `/api/challans` | Create a DRAFT or CONFIRMED challan |
| GET | `/api/challans/:id` | Detail, including items, customer, createdBy, related stock movements, calculated `totalAmount` |
| PATCH | `/api/challans/:id` | Edit `customerId` and/or `items` — DRAFT only |
| POST | `/api/challans/:id/confirm` | DRAFT → CONFIRMED, deducts stock |
| POST | `/api/challans/:id/cancel` | DRAFT/CONFIRMED → CANCELLED, restores stock if it was CONFIRMED |

No `DELETE` endpoint, matching the project's status-based (non-destructive) pattern used
throughout.

### Create

```json
POST /api/challans
{
  "customerId": "…",
  "status": "DRAFT",
  "items": [
    { "productId": "…", "quantity": 5 },
    { "productId": "…", "quantity": 2 }
  ]
}
```
`201` with the created challan (including snapshots and calculated `totalAmount`), or `400`
for bad input (missing/invalid customer or product, non-positive quantity, duplicate product,
empty items, inactive product), or `409` if `status: "CONFIRMED"` was requested and stock
confirmation fails (see "Assumptions" below — in that case **nothing is created at all**).

### Edit (DRAFT only)

```json
PATCH /api/challans/:id
{ "items": [{ "productId": "…", "quantity": 10 }] }
```
Supplying `items` fully replaces the challan's line items (new snapshots, recalculated
`totalQuantity`). `400` if `status` is included in the body (use `/confirm` or `/cancel`
instead). `409` if the challan isn't DRAFT. `404` if it doesn't exist.

### Confirm / Cancel

```
POST /api/challans/:id/confirm   → 200 with the updated challan, or 409/404
POST /api/challans/:id/cancel    → 200 with the updated challan, or 409/404
```

## Validation

- `customerId`: required on create, must reference an existing customer.
- `items`: required, non-empty array; each `productId` must reference an existing, **active**
  product; each `quantity` must be a positive integer; **no product may appear twice** in the
  same request (rejected with a clear message naming the duplicated product).
- `status` (create only): `DRAFT` or `CONFIRMED` — `CANCELLED` is rejected (a challan can't be
  created pre-cancelled).
- `PATCH` rejects `id`, `challanNumber`, `status`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `confirmedAt`,
  `createdById`, `totalQuantity` if present in the body.

## Error handling

| Status | When |
|---|---|
| 400 | Bad input: invalid customer/product reference, inactive product *at create/edit time*, non-positive quantity, duplicate product, empty items, forbidden field in body |
| 401 | Missing/invalid JWT |
| 403 | Authenticated but role isn't permitted for this action |
| 404 | Challan (or, on create, an unrelated resource) not found |
| 409 | The challan's *current state* conflicts with the requested transition: not DRAFT when editing/confirming, already cancelled, insufficient stock, product became inactive since the draft was created |
| 500 | Unexpected error — never leaks stack traces, SQL, or internals |

Note the deliberate 400 vs. 409 split for "inactive product": referencing an inactive product
when **creating or editing** a challan is bad input (400 — you gave us bad data). A product
that **was** active when a draft was made but has since been deactivated, discovered when
**confirming**, is a state conflict (409 — the world changed since you drafted this).

## Assumptions (things the case study / planning docs left unspecified)

These were resolved via your explicit approval before implementation, not invented silently:

1. **Role permissions** — ADMIN+SALES full access, WAREHOUSE+ACCOUNTS read-only. The case
   study only mandates that Sales can create/confirm; everything else here is an approved
   business decision.
2. **Cancellation stock-reversal** — approved: CONFIRMED→CANCELLED restores stock via reversal
   `StockMovement` records; DRAFT→CANCELLED does nothing (nothing was ever deducted).
3. **Creating a challan pre-confirmed, but stock turns out insufficient** — `docs/REQUIREMENTS.md`'s
   language ("reject the entire operation... keep the challan DRAFT") most directly describes
   confirming an *existing* DRAFT via `POST /:id/confirm`, where that's exactly what happens.
   For `POST /api/challans` with `status: "CONFIRMED"` requested at creation time, this
   implementation treats the whole create-and-confirm as one all-or-nothing operation: if stock
   confirmation fails, the transaction rolls back and **no challan is created at all** (not even
   as a DRAFT), rather than silently persisting an unrequested Draft. This was chosen because a
   `POST` that partially succeeds is a worse API contract than one that fully succeeds or fully
   fails — flagging this explicitly since it's an interpretation of ambiguous wording, not a
   literal instruction.
4. **Editing a DRAFT's line items** — implemented as a full replace (`PATCH` with `items`
   deletes and recreates all `ChallanItem` rows) rather than incremental add/remove, since it
   reuses the same snapshot-resolution logic as create and matches a "repeatable line-item
   editor" UI more simply than a diff-based PATCH would.
5. **Persisted total amount** — deliberately not added to the schema; `totalAmount` is always
   calculated from `SUM(lineTotal)` at read time, per your explicit instruction.

## Frontend

Three pages, following the Customer CRM / Inventory conventions (same `Layout`,
`ProtectedRoute`, `AuthContext`, `api.ts`):

- **`/challans`** (`ChallanListPage`) — table, status filter, challan-number search,
  pagination, loading/empty/error states. "+ New Challan" hidden for WAREHOUSE/ACCOUNTS.
- **`/challans/new`** (`ChallanFormPage`) — customer selector, repeatable product+quantity line
  editor (only active products selectable), live per-line and total calculations, "Save Draft"
  / "Save & Confirm" buttons.
- **`/challans/:id/edit`** (`ChallanFormPage`, DRAFT only) — same form, single "Save Changes"
  button; redirects away if the challan isn't DRAFT or the user lacks write access.
- **`/challans/:id`** (`ChallanDetailPage`) — header (number, customer, status, created/confirmed
  by/date), item snapshots with calculated total, related stock movements, and Confirm/Edit
  (DRAFT only) / Cancel (DRAFT or CONFIRMED) actions — all hidden for WAREHOUSE/ACCOUNTS.

`frontend/src/lib/challans.ts` centralizes all API calls (list/get/create/update/confirm/cancel);
`frontend/src/lib/permissions.ts` gained a `canWriteChallans(role)` helper mirroring the
`canWriteInventory` pattern already established.
